newsitem.title: USA: Tyco International to buy ElectroStar.
newsitem.headline: Tyco International to buy ElectroStar.

text.p: Tyco International Ltd., an industrial and commercial products manufacturer, said Friday it had agreed to acquire circuit board maker ElectroStar Inc. in a cash deal valued at $106 million.

Tyco said it would launch an offer of $14 a share for ElectroStar's 7.5 million shares. The offer would be followed by a merger in which each remaining ElectroStar share would be exchanged for $14 in cash.
The stock of Logan, Utah-based ElectroStar closed at $13 Wednesday.
Tyco said the deal would make an immediate contribution to earnings.

Tyco, based in Exeter, N.H., earlier this month said it would buy three metal and framing makers: T.J. Cope, headquartered in Collegeville, Pa.; Unistrut-Europe of Bedford, England; and Steel Support Systems in Birmingham, England. The terms of those deals were not disclosed.
Tyco, which operates in 50 countries, has revenues in excess of $6 billion. Its stock closed at $54.50 Wednesday.
